english.english_feedback:
In July, Ellis began choosing books about rivers and minibeasts during quiet reading and often asked an adult to read the same page twice. By August, Ellis was pointing to repeated words such as “splash” and “stop” and joining in when the group read them aloud. During a September library visit, Ellis retold most of The Little Red Hen to a friend using the pictures, and added a new ending in which every animal shared the bread.

Ellis now writes the first sound of familiar words independently, for example “b” for bee and “s” for sun, and asked for help with longer words when labelling a garden map. In October, Ellis dictated a three-sentence story about a beaver building a dam, then copied the title using the alphabet strip as a guide. When a friend’s idea differed, Ellis listened and included it in the story after a reminder to take turns. Ellis is beginning to notice rhyme in songs and suggested “log” and “frog” during circle time, though rhyming words are still easier to hear than to produce.
